synopsis: Across Chapters 5 and 6, CVPR 2025 is associated with SplatAD, a neural reconstruction and Gaussian-splatting approach that renders both lidar and camera outputs; the cited evidence is on-road [f3814, f4516]. Chapter 6 adds that it models rolling shutter, lidar intensity and ray dropout in real time [f4516]. SplatAD reports training in about one hour per scene on one A100 and claims rendering about an order of magnitude faster than NeRF methods [f4944, f4945]. The cited NeRF baselines render 9.7–28.2 megapixels per second after 0.9–2.6 hours of training; these facts do not establish equivalent performance for heavy off-road applications [f4946, f3814, f4516].

relations.note: Adds Gaussian-splatting implementation and real-time sensor effects to the reconstruction example.
Quantifies scene-training time and hardware for the reconstruction method.
Adds a claimed rendering-speed advantage over NeRF methods.
Provides baseline rendering throughput and training times underlying the NeRF comparison.
